## Further Reading

Alles, M., Brennan, G., Kogan, A., & Vasarhelyi, M. A. (2006). Continuous monitoring of business process controls: A pilot implementation of a continuous auditing system at Siemens. *International Journal of Accounting Information Systems*, *7*(2), 137–161. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.accinf.2005.10.004> A report on a system that monitors business process controls for an internal audit department, running with read-only access on top of the company's enterprise system. The authors found that much more of the audit program could be formalized than expected, and that preventing floods of alarms was a critical task, two lessons for any query library that runs its tests every period.

Huang, F., Cho, S., Lee, K., & No, W. G. (2025). Examining the effectiveness and efficiency of full population testing versus traditional sampling. *Accounting Horizons*, *39*(4), 123–141. <https://doi.org/10.2308/horizons-2022-177> An application of full-population testing to substantive tests of purchase transactions, compared with traditional sampling of the same data. The authors find full-population testing more effective and more efficient at identifying problematic transactions, and discuss its costs and what to consider before adopting it.

Kogan, A., Alles, M. G., Vasarhelyi, M. A., & Wu, J. (2014). Design and evaluation of a continuous data level auditing system. *Auditing: A Journal of Practice & Theory*, *33*(4), 221–245. <https://doi.org/10.2308/ajpt-50844> A framework for auditing procurement data continuously, simulated on a large sample from a health care provider. Its first layer tests compliance with deterministic business rules, like the match and approval tests of Tutorial 12.2, and its second monitors the process analytically. The paper distinguishes the exceptions of the first layer from the anomalies of the second.

No, W. G., Lee, K., Huang, F., & Li, Q. (2019). Multidimensional audit data selection (MADS): A framework for using data analytics in the audit data selection process. *Accounting Horizons*, *33*(3), 127–140. <https://doi.org/10.2308/acch-52453> A framework for the problem that follows full-population testing: tests that flag more items than an auditor can investigate. It identifies problematic items across the whole population and then prioritizes them, so that the auditor's work goes to the items with the highest risk of material misstatement.

Public Company Accounting Oversight Board. (2024). *Amendments related to aspects of designing and performing audit procedures that involve technology-assisted analysis of information in electronic form* (PCAOB Release No. 2024-007). <https://assets.pcaobus.org/pcaob-dev/docs/default-source/rulemaking/docket-052/2024-007-adoptingrelease.pdf> The release that amended the PCAOB's standards on audit evidence and on responses to risk, effective for audits of fiscal years beginning on or after December 15, 2025. Among other things, it specifies considerations for investigating the items that a test of details identifies, and the auditor's responsibilities for evaluating the reliability of information that the company provides in electronic form.

Tojiboyev, N., Appelbaum, D., Kogan, A., & Vasarhelyi, M. A. (2022). Basics of SQL for audit data retrieval and analysis. *Journal of Emerging Technologies in Accounting*, *19*(1), 237–265. <https://doi.org/10.2308/jeta-2020-021> A teaching note on using SQL queries to retrieve audit evidence directly from an enterprise dataset, in Microsoft Access, so that the auditor does not depend on the formatting of reports prepared by others and can begin the analysis sooner.
